 Amit Sana reflects on Indian Idol journey, hopes to collaborate with Abhijeet Sawant again 
 By
 TNM (With ANI Inputs) 
 ✓
 24 October 2026, 6:17 pm 
 4 min read
 24 Oct 2026 
 ANI Photo | Amit Sana reflects on Indian Idol journey, hopes to collaborate with Abhijeet Sawant again 
 Returning to the stage for Indian Idol Legends Return after 22 years, singer Amit Sana discussed his experiences since the first season of Indian Idol, addressing long-standing debates about the show’s outcome, his relationship with winner Abhijeet Sawant, and challenges he faced that kept him from the spotlight.
 Sana, a finalist in the inaugural season, acknowledged that he considered himself equally deserving of the title but accepted the result, emphasising the role of voting in determining the winner. He said, “I will not differ on the fact that I was equally deserving as a winner during the show, but then it’s all about voting and everything. So, at the end of the day, one person has to win.” He declined to revisit allegations of irregularities in the voting process, stating, “It’s something which happened 22 years back. So, it’s not relevant also now either,” and reflected that music is a lifelong journey and every voice is beautiful.

 Sana expressed a desire to work with Sawant again, noting public interest in their reunion. He compared their partnership to notable industry duos, saying, “Me and Abhijeet, we want to work with each other again because we are both good artists and people love us both. And they want to see us together. That’s what I feel. I feel we are like the Salman and Shah Rukh of the music industry.” Their return to the franchise involves paired performances as part of the duet format.
 Also reunited with fellow contestant Prajakta Shukre, Sana reflected on revisiting the show’s set as an opportunity to relive memories from their time preparing and performing together in the first season in 2005.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Discussing his career path post-Indian Idol, Sana described the difficulties he faced transitioning from his upbringing in Bhilai, Chhattisgarh, to the Mumbai entertainment industry. He recalled arriving in Mumbai as a Bollywood fan, excited about pursuing music, but admitted, “After I achieved so much of fame, like in two to three months, it was like an overnight success.” He identified himself as an introvert unaccustomed to navigating new people and situations alone and remarked on the cultural differences between Bhilai and Mumbai. “I come from a place, Bhilai, which has a very systematic lifestyle; it is very education-oriented and definitely many, many, many years behind Mumbai or any other metro city. So, the exposure in terms of fashion or whether it is knowing things about the world or, behaviour, everything is very small-townish over there. The relationships are different. People are very, very different from what I saw in Mumbai. I am not saying that the people are not good here, but culturally, there is a huge difference between the two places,” he said.
 Sana acknowledged the importance of connections and relationships in the entertainment industry but said he struggled to develop them. “After the first stint in the industry, which was Indian Idol 1, the initial years were good enough. But after that, it’s the connections, the personal equation, because at the end of the day, it’s the connections that actually make you work. So, I actually could not make such connections,” he said.
 Following Indian Idol, Sana released his debut album Chal Diye in 2005, composed by Vishal–Shekhar, and later Yaadein in 2008, composed by Rajiv Bhatt. He described financial losses incurred during the production of his second album, an independent project intended to showcase his musical influences. “Again, I got duped by people during that journey. So, a lot of money got invested into that. And it was not needed as such. And because of that, I incurred some losses. Not because the album was not good,” he explained.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 After this period, Sana focused on live performances but faced challenges adapting to industry changes such as the rise of digital streaming and algorithm-driven music discovery. He also acknowledged that limited engagement within Bollywood hindered his opportunities in playback singing, stating that close collaboration with music producers and directors alongside people skills are crucial for building a film career.
 Reflecting on his career, Sana said he spent significant time understanding his fears, strengths and areas beyond singing. While he admitted that distancing himself from the industry was not ideal, he believes it prepared him for this new phase of his career. “I think this whole time I was just getting ready,” he said.
 Sana revealed plans to release original singles over the next one to two months instead of a full album, stating, “I also want to come up with my own songs, which I have taken time out this year. Yeah, I have composed some really nice songs, and they have been waiting for a long time.”
 Hosted by Aditya Narayan, Indian Idol Legends Return features judge Himesh Reshammiya and pairs popular singers from previous seasons for a musical competition. Participants include Salman Ali and Mohammad Danish, Devender Pal Singh and Mayuri Saha, Swaroopp Khan and Ritika Raj, Prajakta Shukre and Amit Sana, Senjuti Das and Nihal Tauro, Subhajit Chakraborty and Bidipta Chakraborty, Ashish Kulkarni and Sayli Kamble Patil, Tanishk Shukla and Myscmme Bosu, Anshika Chonkar and Rishi Singh, Manraj Veer and Manasi Ghosh, Ankush Bhardwaj and Sireesha Bhagavatula, and Abhijeet Sawant and Chetna Bhardwaj.
 The season premiered on October 17 and airs on Sony Entertainment Television and Sony LIV on Saturdays and Sundays at 8 pm.
